Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the MediCore Devices Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you may press star then one on your telephone. Please note, this call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements, including expectations regarding our future performance, business outlook, and financial results. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Joining me on today's call are Mike Reynolds, CEO; Sarah Chen, CFO; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; and Tom Hargrove, Chief Commercial Officer.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Mike Reynolds.

Mike Reynolds:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. MediCore Devices delivered strong results this quarter, driven by increasing adoption of our innovative medical devices and strategic partnerships.

Today, I will cover five key aspects of our performance:
1. Procedure volume trends and market recovery commentary
2. Inventory management and working capital optimization
3. R&D investment and innovation pipeline progress
4. Overall performance highlights and key achievements
5. Revenue and margin guidance for the next quarter/year

Sarah will then provide a more detailed review of our financials. After that, we'll open the call for your questions.

Now, let's get started with procedure volume trends and market recovery commentary.

As we look at the details, procedure volume trends and our outlook for market recovery stand out as critical drivers of our performance in the medical devices sector. Globally, procedure volumes across our key franchises grew 14% year-over-year on an organic, constant-currency basis, accelerating from the 11% growth in Q2. This is our fifth straight quarter of double-digit expansion, signaling a strong rebound in elective and semi-elective procedures after pandemic setbacks.

By franchise, our Cardiovascular segment, about 45% of total revenue, saw procedure volumes surge 18% year-over-year. TAVR volumes jumped 22%, powered by adoption of our next-generation Evolut FX platform, which commands a 32% U.S. market share based on the latest CRT implant tracking data. Expanded indications for lower-risk patients mean over 65% of our TAVR cases are now in low- or intermediate-risk profiles, up from 52% last year. Coronary interventions with our Resolute Onyx drug-eluting stent rose 15%, thanks to its superior deliverability in complex PCI. In electrophysiology, procedures using our Affera mapping system with AI-enhanced signal processing grew 16%, as hospitals focus on rhythm management with rising atrial fibrillation cases.

Orthopedics, our second-largest franchise at 28% of revenue, achieved 12% volume growth. Knee procedures increased 14%, led by the Persona IQ smart knee system—the first FDA-cleared connected implant—driving 25% adoption in ambulatory surgery centers. Hip volumes were up 10%, with some moderation from Mako robotic utilization at 85% in high-volume centers as customers absorb prior capital spends. Our Rosa Shoulder application for reverse shoulder arthroplasty gained traction, with early Q3 volumes up 30% sequentially.

Neuromodulation and Structural Heart volumes advanced 13% and 20%, respectively. Incepta ICDs benefited from Micra leadless pacemaker synergies, gaining share in the subcutaneous ICD market, while the Hugo RAS system's soft tissue procedures reached 1,200 cases globally, up 40% year-over-year as we ramp toward 150 systems installed by end of 2024.

Regionally, the U.S. led with 16% growth, now 5% ahead of 2019 pre-COVID levels, supported by pent-up demand and Medicare's 2024 IPPS updates boosting ASC payments by 3.2%. EMEA grew 9%, despite reimbursement challenges in Germany where TAVR DRG rates are flat, and U.K. NHS backlogs from industrial action. French TAVI registry data shows volumes at 102% of 2019, and we're optimistic about Italy's PNRR-funded upgrades accelerating second-half growth. APAC shone at 19%, with China's NEP volume-based procurement stabilizing after price pressures—our domestic TAVR partner volumes up 28%. Japan added via strong EP adoption, and India's ASC expansion helped orthopedics.

On recovery, we now see full-year 2024 global procedure volumes hitting 107% of 2019 levels industry-wide, up from our prior 105% view. Aging demographics—with the over-65 population up 3% year-over-year—plus procedure-enabling tech support this. Our U.S. and Singapore facilities hit 99% on-time delivery, countering nitinol and bioabsorbable polymer inflation.

Strategically, we're pushing digital ecosystems like our Procedure Analytics platform integrated with Apple HealthKit and Epic, achieving 40% attach rates on new Mako systems, cutting OR case times by 12%. We're accelerating RAS with Hugo's FDA IDE approval for general surgery, eyeing a $15 billion market to challenge da Vinci's dominance. Sustainability with 30% recycled packaging has won preferred status in three major U.S. GPOs.

For Q4, we expect volumes up 13-15% year-over-year, ASPs stable at 1-2% on mix. U.S. recession risks loom for commercial ortho, but 85% recurring revenue from services and disposables buffers us. We're set to outperform as procedures normalize and innovation premiumizes.

Now, let's talk about inventory management and working capital optimization.

Before diving deeper into segments, our progress here drove a 12% year-over-year free cash flow improvement to $285 million in Q3. In med devices—from capital like NaviGuide robotic systems akin to da Vinci, to consumables like CardioFlow stents and BioShield catheters—inventory stewardship is vital amid FDA/EU MDR traceability, biologics perishability, and chip shortages.

Our trailing 12-month inventory turnover hit 4.2x, up from 3.5x a year ago and above the 3.8x industry median per Deloitte. Days Inventory Outstanding fell to 87 days quarter-end, 15% better sequentially from 102 and 17% from last year's 105—outpacing Stryker and Boston Scientific's 95-110 days.

By category: Consumables (52% of value) turnover to 6.8x from 5.9x, cutting excess 22% and avoiding $14 million obsolescence amid 8-10% polymer inflation. Capital equipment DIO to 120 from 140, matching hospital capex cycles post-recovery. Implants and biologics at 65 days from 78, via just-in-time for OrthoFlex 3D-printed titanium.

This trimmed our cash conversion cycle 12 days to 68, DSO steady at 52 via Vizient/Premier GPOs, DPO to 87 without supplier strain.

We've spent $45 million on Supply Chain 4.0 with SAP S/4HANA and Blue Yonder AI, lifting SKU forecast accuracy to 92% from 84%—key for EP demand swings from trials or recalls like Abbott's MitraClip.

Enablers: RFID/IoT in 85% of 45 global DCs cut discrepancies 18%, sterile cycle counts 40%. VMI with DuPont/TSMC covers 35% raw materials, shifting $120 million risk upstream like Medtronic. Consignment/scan-to-own for ortho/neurovascular like NeuroGuard cut owned inventory 25%, speeding recognition. Digital twins via Siemens NX preempted 15% stockouts during Red Sea issues.

U.S. (65% sales) DIO 82 days post-restocking, TAVR growth without builds. Europe (18%) at 105 days from MDR, but Ireland manufacturing freed €25 million. APAC ex-China/China saw India EP up 28%, Singapore hub cut 30%, NMPA stents lead times to 9 weeks at 5.1x turnover.

Inventory builds our moat—over-optimization risks stockouts like 2022 monitoring surges; excess hits R&D. ROIC to 14.2% from 12.1%, working capital 14% of sales vs. sector 17%.

Ahead, blockchain via IBM Hyperledger targets 10 more DIO days by year-end, freeing $400 million for M&A like neuromodulation tuck-ins and buybacks—fortifying against 11% raw inflation and geopolitics.

Moving on to R&D investment and innovation pipeline progress.

Our R&D is core to long-term growth in the $500 billion med devices market, targeting structural heart, neuromodulation, robotics, AI diagnostics amid 8-12% CAGR procedures through 2030 per iData and Evaluate.

Q3 R&D spend was $285 million, 14.8% of revenue—up from 13.2% prior year, on track for 14-16% full-year. Trailing 12 months hit $1.15 billion, 17% up, outpacing revenue vs. Abbott's 12%, Boston's 13.5%. Allocation: 45% structural heart/CV, 25% neuromod/ neurovascular, 20% robotics/digital, 10% ortho/bioresorbables—yielding 2.5x EBITDA margin lift via 20-30% launch margins.

Pipeline: 22 programs, 6 late-stage—up from 18. Q3 had 12 milestones, two FDA IDEs, strong first-in-human.

Flagships: VitaFlow Neo TAVR—next-gen on 50,000-implant platform—finished U.S. IDE enrollment (n=450), 12-month data 95% safety, 2.2% leak beating Evolut. PMA Q1 2025, CE low-risk underway; $800M peak in $8B 15% CAGR market.

NeuroPulse RF for hypertension ($15B market): 6-month pivotal (n=300) showed 18 mmHg BP drop sustained, zero SAEs. China NMPA, U.S. PMA Q4 2024; like ReCor's Paradise.

RoboAssist single-port for urologic/gyne: Europe first-in-human, 25% faster times, 30% less blood loss. U.S. IDE 50 sites, 4.8/5 ergonomics. Philips imaging partnership boosts AI.

AI-Dx CardioWear patch: FDA 510(k) for AFib, 98% sensitivity vs. Apple Watch. Q1 2025 U.S./EU launch, $200M SaaS run-rate FY2026 in $50B monitoring.

U.S. 60% spend, 90% FDA alignment; 4 CE Marks YTD Europe; Asia China +35%, fast-tracks; EM India/LATAM ortho trials.

Platforms like Modular Heart cut costs 25%, IP 450+ patents (15% AI). Siemens $150M deal shares 30% costs.

FY2024 R&D $1.2-1.25B (15% growth), H2 5-7 catalysts: PMAs, trials, launches. Drives 12-15% 2025 growth, 25% new-product ROIC vs. 18% WACC.

Next, overall performance highlights and key achievements.

These underscore robust execution amid MedTech dynamics, ahead of Medtronic/Boston Scientific. Revenue hit $1.28 billion, up 18% year-over-year and 6% organic constant-currency—beating guidance/consensus by 4%, ninth double-digit quarter. Driven by 12% procedural rise, 2% ASP from premium mix. Adjusted EPS $1.92, +22%, beat by $0.15 on leverage.

Gross margins +250 bps to 69.2% via Costa Rica Greenfield efficiencies and Robotics/AI mix (+45% YoY). Operating margins 29.8%, +320 bps, SG&A <30% first time via sales tools. FCF $420M (33% revenue), cash $2.1B, net debt/EBITDA 0.8x.

Franchise wins: Cardiovascular (42%) +22% to $535M; ApexFlow TAVR 18% U.S. share, 15,000 implants +35%, EchoGuide cut times 22%; FlexPulse EP +28%, 95% success.

Ortho/Spine (25%) +15% to $320M vs. peers' softness; ApexKnee robotics 65% attach (from 45%), OrthoNav AI; FDA bioresorbable spinal clearance for $2.5B fusion.

Robotics/Digital (18%) +52% to $230M; ApexBot CE Mark EMEA launch, $150M backlog; SwarmAI cuts OR turnaround 30%, throughput 25%.

Diagnostics/Wearables +15% to $195M; VitalSense CGM 12% Type 2 share vs. Dexcom/Abbott, Apple integration 40% retention, Roche pump partnership.

Regions: U.S. 62% +21% on IPPS TAVR boost 3.5%, 98% sales quota. EMEA +14% navigating MDR/Germany/UK via local mfg. APAC +32% ($195M), China +48% NMPA ApexFlow, India +60% ortho.

'Precision Growth 2027': R&D +25% to $185M (14.5%), 14 late-stage incl. neural interface. Supply resilience 95%, 50% recyclable packaging. $750M NeuroStim M&A +$80M synergies.

Q3 validates value-based leadership; raising FY2024 revenue $5.15-5.25B (17-19%), EPS $7.45-7.55.

Finally, revenue and margin guidance for the next quarter/year.

For Q4 ending Dec 31, revenue $1.24-1.27B, organic 7-9% up (2pt FX headwind USD/euro/yen). Structural Heart $580-600M +10-13%, U.S. TAVR share 28% Millennium, AetherFlow Ultra low-calcification, CMS low-risk. Endovascular/Peripheral $420-440M flat-4%, FlexiStent Nano Breakthrough offsets DCB scrutiny. Emerging (Neuro/Robotics) $240-250M +18-22%, PulseSync U.S. launch, AetherBot CE AI nav.

Regions: U.S. 75% 9-11%; EMEA 15% 5-7% NICE/Germany; APAC ex-China 6%, China flat w/$50M backlog.

Margins: Gross 68.5-69.5% (+100-200 bps) scale Galway, titanium -15%; Op 25.0-25.8% $20M SG&A/R&D wind-down.

FY2025 revenue $5.15-5.35B, 8-11% organic midpoint (stable macro, mid-single procedures IQVIA). Structural Heart $2.45-2.55B 11-14%; Endo/Peri $1.75-1.82B 5-8%; Emerging $1.00-1.05B 20-25%.

Drivers: AetherFlow Ultra 40k units, V-Wave shunt trials Q2, AetherBot AI precision vs. Hugo/Mako. M&A EP bolt-ons post-VascuTech. Nearshoring 85% components.

Regions: U.S. 10% boomers; EMEA/APAC 8%, China H1 ramp; 1-2pt FX.

Margins: Gross 69-70% +150 bps Galway/resins; Op 25.5-26.5%, EPS $4.85-5.15 (25% tax, $300M buybacks).

Risks: CMS OPPS TAVR, Abbott launches; upside PulseSync +$100M, MDR ahead.

Confident in growth/margins via pipeline/ops.

I will now turn the call over to Sarah for a review of our financial results.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Mike. As Mike outlined, we delivered a strong financial performance this quarter. Revenue of $1.28 billion grew 18% reported, 6% organic, with procedural strength across franchises. Gross profit expanded to 69.2%, up 250 basis points from manufacturing scale and premium mix, while operating expenses were controlled tightly, yielding adjusted operating margins of 29.8%. Adjusted EPS of $1.92 beat expectations, reflecting 22% growth. Balance sheet remains rock-solid with $2.1 billion cash, enabling $420 million free cash flow. For FY2024, we're raising guidance to revenue of $5.15 to $5.25 billion and EPS $7.45 to $7.55, incorporating the momentum Mike described.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Dr. Vasquez for an update on our product pipeline.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Sarah. I'm excited to share updates on our innovative pipeline. We recently received FDA clearance for the VitaFlow Neo TAVR system, a groundbreaking next-gen platform promising superior safety and reduced paravalvular leak in structural heart interventions. Building on this, NeuroPulse RF ablation for hypertension showed durable BP reductions in pivotal data, with China launch imminent. RoboAssist Precision Platform advanced with first-in-human success and Philips integration, while AI-Dx CardioWear gained 510(k) for unmatched AFib detection. Our 22 programs, with six late-stage, position us for multiple catalysts ahead, driving premium growth in robotics, neuromodulation, and digital health.

Now, back to Mike for Q&A.

Mike Reynolds:
Thank you, Elena. Operator, we are now ready to take questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for asking questions: press star then one. Our first question comes from John Smith with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Thanks, good morning. Mike, on procedure volumes, the U.S. outperformance to 5% above 2019 is impressive—can you elaborate on sustainability given potential macro slowdowns, especially in ortho?

Mike Reynolds:
Great question, John. Yes, U.S. volumes at 16% growth reflect resolved pent-up demand and IPPS boosts, but our recurring 85% from disposables/services insulates us. Ortho faces commercial softness risks, but ASC shift with Persona IQ at 25% adoption and Rosa Shoulder ramp provide offsets. We see Q4 at 13-15%, well-positioned.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen:
Thanks. Sarah, margins expanded sharply—how much from inventory optimization versus mix, and is 70% gross sustainable into FY25?

Sarah Chen:
Hi Lisa. Inventory gains shaved DIO to 87 days, freeing cash and reducing obsolescence, contributing about 100 basis points alongside 150 from Costa Rica scale and high-margin robotics at 45% growth. FY25 gross guide 69-70% assumes continued efficiencies like titanium dual-sourcing and resin stabilization—yes, sustainable at midpoint with pipeline launches.

Mike Reynolds:
Thank you for that insight, Sarah.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Patel with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Mike Patel:
Good morning. Tom, APAC was a standout at 19% volumes—thoughts on China stabilization and India opportunity amid procurement dynamics?

Tom Hargrove:
Morning, Mike. China NEP stabilized post-price erosion, with TAVR partner +28% and NMPA stents cutting leads to 9 weeks. India's ASC buildout and EP +28% add tailwinds for ortho bundles—EM like India at +60% revenues shows our localization pays off. Expect APAC to drive FY25 outsized growth.

Mike Reynolds:
Thank you for that insight, Tom.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Lee with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Sarah Lee:
Thanks. Elena, the pipeline milestones are robust—timeline risks on VitaFlow Neo PMA or RoboAssist IDE, and competitive moat versus da Vinci?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thanks, Sarah. VitaFlow Neo IDE data exceeds Evolut benchmarks—on track Q1 2025 PMA with 90% FDA alignment. RoboAssist first-in-human beat ergonomics scores, Philips AI edges da Vinci in endo suites with 25% faster times. Modular platforms derisk, 450+ IP incl. AI protect moat for $10B market share.

Mike Reynolds:
Thank you for your questions. Before we conclude, I want to thank our employees, customers, and partners for their continued support. We are confident in our ability to continue delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders.

Thank you for joining us today.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
